learningObjectives.title: Structure 3.1 The periodic table and periodicity

questions.q: Elements in the modern periodic table are arranged in order of increasing:
questions.explain: Elements are ordered by proton (atomic) number, with similar elements falling in the same group.

questions.q: Elements in the same group of the periodic table have:
options: The same number of valence (outer) electrons
questions.explain: Shared valence electron number gives similar chemical properties within a group.

questions.q: A horizontal row of the periodic table is called a:
questions.explain: Across a period, the number of occupied electron shells stays the same while nuclear charge increases.

questions.q: Across a period from left to right, atomic radius generally:
questions.explain: Increasing nuclear charge (with electrons in the same shell) pulls electrons in more strongly, shrinking the atom.

questions.q: Down a group, atomic radius generally:
questions.explain: Additional electron shells outweigh the greater nuclear charge, so atoms get larger down a group.

questions.q: First ionization energy generally increases across a period because:
options: Nuclear charge increases while electrons enter the same shell
Electrons are added to new shells
questions.explain: Stronger attraction to the nucleus makes electrons harder to remove across a period.

questions.q: Which element has the largest first ionization energy?
questions.explain: Ionization energy increases across a period and up a group, so fluorine (top-right area) is highest among these.

questions.q: Down a group, first ionization energy generally:
questions.explain: Outer electrons are further from the nucleus and better shielded, so they are removed more easily.

questions.q: Electronegativity is a measure of:
options: An atom's ability to attract a shared pair of electrons in a bond
The energy to remove an electron
questions.explain: Electronegativity increases across a period and decreases down a group.

questions.q: Which is the most electronegative element?
questions.explain: Fluorine is the most electronegative element on the Pauling scale.

questions.q: The elements in Group 1 (alkali metals) become more reactive down the group because:
options: The outer electron is lost more easily as atoms get larger
questions.explain: Increased distance and shielding lower the ionization energy, so reactivity increases down Group 1.

questions.q: Group 17 (halogens) become less reactive down the group because:
options: It becomes harder to attract an extra electron as atoms get larger
questions.explain: Greater atomic radius and shielding reduce the attraction for an incoming electron down Group 17.

questions.q: Elements in the centre block of the periodic table (Groups 3-12) are the:
questions.explain: The d-block transition metals often show variable oxidation states and coloured compounds.

questions.q: Metallic character generally increases:
options: Down a group and to the left across a period
Up a group and to the right
Across a period to the right
questions.explain: Metals are found to the left and bottom; non-metals to the top right.

questions.q: Oxides of elements on the left of a period (metals) tend to be:
questions.explain: Metal oxides are typically basic; non-metal oxides (right of a period) are typically acidic.

questions.q: The noble gases (Group 18) are very unreactive because they have:
questions.explain: A complete valence shell gives a stable configuration with little tendency to react.

questions.q: An element in Period 3, Group 2 would have the electron configuration:
questions.explain: Two outer electrons in the third shell (magnesium) place it in Period 3, Group 2.

questions.q: Across period 3, the oxides change from basic to acidic, reflecting the change from:
questions.explain: Left-hand metals form basic oxides; right-hand non-metals form acidic oxides, with amphoteric oxides in between.

questions.q: Which pair of elements would have the most similar chemical properties?
questions.explain: Both are Group 17 halogens with seven valence electrons, so their chemistry is similar.

questions.q: The periodic trend in properties across periods provides evidence for:
options: The repeating pattern of electron configurations
questions.explain: Periodicity arises because valence electron configurations repeat across successive periods.
